findings.text: the row labelled "recorded baseline, cumulative since boot" carries 0.3396 and calls it "the baseline this plan carries", while the plan's section-7 landing record for that baseline states 0.3366 and the baseline table in this same evidence record states 0.3366, so the "moved 2.6 percent since the baseline was recorded" sentence at :1490 is against a figure a reader cannot identify from the record: against 0.3366 the move is 3.5 percent, and the plan carrying two same-boot cumulative readings is not stated.

the sentence "Each gate log's first line names the revision it ran at, the tree and the command" follows a list of four named logs of which two do not carry that header, negative-control-restore.log (first line "source restored to the unmutated revision; same test re-run") and live-interval-read.log (first line "{"), so a reader checking the claim against the named files finds it false for half of them and cannot tell which revision the restored re-run was against.

item_verdicts.diff: read commit by commit against base f3f2cd84; f8921dec adds the span function and its CLI wiring (+57 in the module, +114 in tests, a new eight-case class plus the two command-level cases), and 05741465 adds the evidence section, the SVG and the plan comment, with no change to any other file and no change to the plan-version or plan-modified meta lines.

item_verdicts.goal: the node's goal is a throttled share measured over the interval between two samples so relief is attributable to the period rather than diluted by uptime; imas_ambix/agent/throttling.py:444 computes exactly that from two samples and a stated span, and the live 60-second reading is recorded beside the cumulative ratio.
item_verdicts.manifest: read; it records both commits, the four logs, the live reading, the receipt with its IDENTICAL first-line check, a restore re-run, and three follow-ons including the pre-existing collapse in interval_throttled_share's cause; its statement that the recorded baseline is 0.3396 is the figure the plan's followup text carries but not the one the plan's own section-7 landing record states, which is finding 1.
item_verdicts.write_paths: the declared paths are imas_ambix/agent/throttling.py, tests/agent/test_throttling.py, docs/evidence/archive/slurm-hosted-agent-fleet-landed.html, docs/figures/slurm-hosted-agent-fleet and docs/plans/slurm-hosted-agent-fleet.html; git show --stat for f8921dec and 05741465 lists exactly five files and every one is inside them.

justifications.durability: tests/agent/test_throttling.py:351 fails if the span stops entering the denominator and :359 fails if the figure is taken from the cumulative counters, but the command-level emission of share_over_elapsed is asserted only where the span's rise is zero, so a wiring that mis-scaled a positive span would not redden the suite.
justifications.evidence: the interval figure re-derives exactly from the counters the run states (55,743,624 / 240,000,000 = 0.232265) and every named gate has a log whose first line names revision 05741465, but the baseline the evidence table labels "recorded baseline" is 0.3396 while the plan's landing record and the evidence record's baseline table both state 0.3366 (finding 1), and one named log is claimed to carry a header it does not (finding 2).
justifications.fit: imas_ambix/agent/throttling.py:469-478 follows interval_delta's ValueError refusal style and :582 serialises through the Unmeasured value strings _counters_payload at :512 already uses, and no added name carries a plan, sprint or version label.
justifications.goal_fidelity: imas_ambix/agent/throttling.py:444 and :574 deliver the goal and the recorded reading at the span sits beside the cumulative one, with the only withheld point the provenance of the baseline figure it is compared against.

raw_text:
Independent review of run r-20260922T183129460322-fleet-throttle-delta (node
fleet-throttle-delta), plan imas-ambix:slurm-hosted-agent-fleet section 7, commits
f8921dec and 05741465 against base f3f2cd84. Read: the dispatch, the manifest, both
commit diffs, the four gate logs, the negative-control receipt and its restore log, the
landed evidence section and the plan comment block. Re-checked here, and nothing else:
the interval arithmetic re-derived from the raw counters the run itself states, the
negative control's receipt read against the declared string, and the shipped refusal
conditions read at their lines. No file in the reviewed tree was modified, and the
focused suite was not re-run (its own log names the revision it ran at).

Q(a) Does the returned figure match what the fence defines? YES.
imas_ambix/agent/throttling.py:479-481 takes the ceiling's core count as quota over
period, multiplies by the stated span in microseconds, and divides the interval rise in
throttled_usec by that capacity. The ceiling comes from the earlier sample, as
interval_throttled_share at :443 does, so the denominator describes the quota in force
while the counters accumulated. The span considered is the far sample's, not a
mid-span quota change, which the docstring at :444-466 states.

Q(b) Does it refuse where the fence says it must, and only there. YES.
Four refusals at their lines: a span beginning in a group with no stated ceiling
(:469-471), a span that is not positive (:473), a sample stating no period counters
(:476-478), and a counter going backwards, delegated to interval_delta's own refusal at
:405-411. Each raises ValueError rather than substituting a number, so the
absent-versus-genuinely-zero distinction the module already draws is carried through.
The command at :574 catches that ValueError and states the cause as an Unmeasured value
string, which is the same serialisation _counters_payload at :512 already uses for the
cumulative field; the function refuses and the CLI reports, and the fence asks the
function to refuse.

Q(c) Can the live figure be re-derived from the counters the run states? YES.
The recorded log and the evidence section state the span's counters as usage_usec
+174,225,595, nr_periods +600, nr_throttled +157, throttled_usec +55,743,624, with
cpu.max 400000 100000 and a 60.0 s span. 55,743,624 / (4 x 60.0 x 1e6) = 0.232265,
which is the emitted 0.23226480429229585 and the recorded 0.2323. The 600 periods over
60.0 s at one period per 100 ms is an independent check that the span's own accounting
agrees with the wall clock it was divided by. The login-node boot_id in the run's live
read (82c41dfa-...) is the one the evidence record's earlier login-side reading carries,
so the two cumulative figures compared there are from one boot and their difference is
a movement rather than a reboot artefact.

Q(d) Is the recorded negative control the declared one? YES.
The declared string is "treat an absent period counter as a zero when differencing the
two samples, instead of refusing; the refusal test for a sample stating no counters must
then fail". The receipt's first line repeats it verbatim; the applied mutation is to
interval_delta's unaccounted branch, which is the branch the phrase names; the named
test fails with "Failed: DID NOT RAISE <class 'ValueError'>", which is the refusal
receipt and not a mis-specified expectation; and the restore log re-runs the class to 8
passed. The mutation is discriminating: it is the one branch whose removal turns that
refusal into a zero.
